# #3699: Patch: follow-up to #3682 from the after-merge spot-check
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

<!-- jackioh-bot:spot-check-follow-up #3682 -->
The after-merge spot-check of #3682 ([run](https://github.com/Jlore-Studios/JackiOh/actions/runs/42973450742)) found 1 blocking problem(s) in the change as it merged (`3a3de664a2af`). `claude-1` (claude, `opus`, strong) reviewed it. #3682 stays merged: nothing is reverted, and this issue fixes what it found in a change of its own, from `main`.

## What to fix

- [ ] `apps/web/src/net/first-load.test.ts:91`: Since #3682, the #3499 test 'no built script, a worker's included, holds patch-meta.ts's disk reader' can no longer fail: a Vite bundle without `patchMeta()` now resolves `#jackioh-patch-meta` to `patch-meta.browser.ts`, which statically imports the whole 650 KB `patches.json`, and the test's probe string is not in that file, so the bloat it guards against now ships with every test green.
  Evidence: The test treats a bundle as a regression only if it contains the literal "holds an entry with no version" (first-load.test.ts:97). Before #3682, a bundle without the plugin (the practice worker's own plugin list, vite.config.ts:57) fell through to `patch-meta.ts`, whose code carries that string, so the test caught it. After #3682, apps/web/package.json maps the `browser` condition to `patch-meta.browser.ts`. Vite's client and worker resolution applies the `browser` condition, so such a bundle now gets the browser file instead. Its error strings are "is not a list of patches", "holds a patch with no version string" and "holds no patches". The PR says it chose them on purpose to keep the probe 'specific to patch-meta.ts'. Its own new comment in vite.config.ts:56 says that without `patchMeta()` the worker would bundle the 650 KB history. The other #3499 guards miss this: the probe-text and gzip tests read only the entry chunk and its preloads (`entryAndPreloads()`), which leaves out worker chunks, and the 'no static import of patches.json' test scans only `src/`, while the browser file sits at the package root. Fix: make the worker test also flag any built script holding a marker that only the browser file carries, such as its "holds a patch with no version string" error, and update the test's comment to name both files.

## Done when

- Each finding above is fixed where it points, or answered with the evidence that it does not hold.
- Every check is green, with no test skipped, ignored or weakened to get there (CLAUDE.md rule 12).
